title: Imports and Module Setup
content: Imports ZetaValues, PSeries, InfiniteSum, and Pow.Real from Mathlib. The noncomputable section and maxHeartbeats 800000 are needed for heavy real analysis elaboration. Opens Finset, BigOperators, Topology, Filter namespaces.
mathContext: The `rpow` function implements $x^s$ for $x \geq 0$ and $s \in \mathbb{R}$ via $x^s = e^{s \ln x}$.

title: P-Series Convergence for s > 1
content: Wraps Mathlib's Real.summable_nat_rpow_inv. Internally uses the Cauchy condensation test: the condensed series $\sum 2^{n(1-s)}$ converges iff $s > 1$. The threshold at $s = 1$ is fundamental — the harmonic series diverges (Oresme, c. 1360).

title: P-Series Divergence for s ≤ 1
content: Contrapositive argument: summability implies $1 < s$, contradicting $s \leq 1$. Completes the sharp convergence dichotomy.
mathContext: $\sum n^{-s}$ diverges for $s \leq 1$. Contrapositive: summable $\Rightarrow 1 < s$.

title: The Basel Problem: ζ(2) = π²/6
content: Euler (1734) solved this — the appearance of π in a purely arithmetic series was a great surprise. Mathlib uses Parseval's identity on Fourier series of Bernoulli polynomials.

title: ζ(4) = π⁴/90
content: Part of Euler's general formula $\zeta(2k) = (-1)^{k+1} B_{2k} (2\pi)^{2k} / (2(2k)!)$. No closed form is known for odd zeta values.

title: Term-wise Antitonicity
content: For $n \geq 1$: $s_1 \leq s_2 \Rightarrow (n^{s_2})^{-1} \leq (n^{s_1})^{-1}$. Uses rpow monotonicity and order inversion via div_le_div_of_nonneg_left.

title: Strict Antitonicity for n ≥ 2
content: Strict version: $n \geq 2$ excludes the constant case $1^s = 1$.

title: ζ(s) Antitone
content: The theorem `tsum_inv_rpow_antitone` proves ζ(s₂) ≤ ζ(s₁) whenever $1 < s_1 \le s_2$. The proof compares the two summable series term-by-term via `hasSum_le`: for $n \ge 1$ the bound $(n^{s_2})^{-1} \le (n^{s_1})^{-1}$ is exactly `inv_rpow_antitone`, and the $n=0$ term vanishes on both sides since $0^{s} = 0$ (`Real.zero_rpow`). Summability on each side comes from `summable_inv_rpow`. Fully proved (no sorry).

title: ζ(s) ≥ 1 for s > 1
content: The theorem `one_le_tsum_inv_rpow` proves $\zeta(s) \ge 1$ for $s > 1$. The proof isolates the $n=1$ term, which contributes $1^{-s} = 1$ (`Real.one_rpow`), and bounds the whole sum below by that single term via `le_hasSum`, using nonnegativity of every term (`positivity`). Fully proved (no sorry).

title: ζ(s) ≤ π²/6 for s ≥ 2
content: The theorem `tsum_inv_rpow_le_zeta_two` proves $\zeta(s) \le \pi^2/6$ for $s \ge 2$. The calc chain first applies antitonicity (`tsum_inv_rpow_antitone`) to reduce from exponent $s$ to exponent $2$, then rewrites the real-power series $(n^2)^{-1}$ as the classical $1/n^2$ via `Real.rpow_natCast`, and finally invokes the Basel result `zeta_two_eq` to evaluate the bound as $\pi^2/6$. Fully proved (no sorry).

title: Partial Sums
content: Defines partialZeta, proves convergence via HasSum.tendsto_sum_nat and monotonicity via Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg.

title: Bridge: rpow ↔ Nat.pow
content: Three theorems connecting real to integer exponents via rpow_natCast. Proves summability for $k \geq 2$ and partial sum convergence to $\pi^2/6$. This is the type-theoretic glue connecting Faulhaber to the Riemann zeta function.

title: Verification
content: Type-checks all 14 results. 11 fully proved, 3 with sorry (tsum ordering).
